display.purpose: The name as h1. It is visible in list view and until the stage is ready. Elsewhere it stays in the document for assistive technology while the form or the still shows the name.

subtitle.purpose: Job titles, the degree, and Competitions.

contact-email.purpose: The email address, the largest link on the site, breaking anywhere so it never overflows.

wordmark.purpose: The name in the navigation bar.

role.purpose: The role line in the first viewport, in Quiet.

lead.purpose: The line that states a result. About paragraphs use the same size at line-height 1.625.

body.purpose: Prose. Dash lists open up to 1.6.

caption.purpose: Technology lists, dates, availability and the footer, in Quiet. Dates use tabular figures.

motion.name: stage-reveal
motion.purpose: The stage fades in over the ground once the canvas is ready.

motion.name: rebuild
motion.value: smoothstep over the last 0.9 viewport, damped at rate 5
motion.purpose: Movement between shapes; the form holds while the words are read.

motion.name: pour-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-point departure, so shapes pour rather than fade.

motion.name: sway
motion.purpose: Slow turn of the form at rest.

motion.name: burst-decay
motion.purpose: How the form settles after a click.

motion.name: streak
motion.value: velocity damped at rate 7, up to 3 scene units

motion.name: reading-dim
motion.value: 0.2 at mid-rebuild on desktop, 0.16 while reading on phones, damped at rate 6
motion.purpose: Keeps the form from competing with the words.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Selects the Still tier and disables smooth scroll and the stage fade.

narrative.overview:
The site is one body of matter. Tens of thousands of points of copper light hold a shape, pour out of it as the visitor scrolls, and settle into the next one: the name, the career, each project, the skills, the degree, and finally an @. There is only ever one form on screen, and it is always the same particles. Nothing is swapped, faded or replaced.

The form is the main event and the words are its plain counterpart. Text sits directly on the warm near-black ground, with no panel, card or tint behind it, and the form takes the space the text leaves free. Every word is server-rendered HTML, so a visitor reaches the facts without waiting on the form.

The form is also one presentation of a plain document. The same words stand beside live particles, beside captured stills, or alone in a list view, and the system holds in all of them.
keyCharacteristics: One form, one set of particles, rebuilt rather than replaced at each stop.
One colour family of copper, amber and ember glow on a warm near-black.
Text directly on the dark ground, with no panels or cards.
A form that answers the visitor: it parts round the cursor, bursts on a click, and streaks on a fast scroll.
Three rendering tiers and a list view, all carrying the same words.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every colour sits in the copper family on near-black. A second hue is a system change, not an accent. The neutrals are warm for the same reason: there is no pure white, pure black or cool grey anywhere.

rules.name: The Amber Answer Rule
rules.body: Amber in the interface only ever answers the visitor: hover and focus, never a resting state. If nothing is being pointed at or focused, no amber shows outside the form.

rules.name: The Form Carries Scale Rule
rules.body: The largest letters on the site are made of particles. HTML type peaks at the Display size, so the words never compete with the form by growing.

rules.name: The Wide Heavy Rule
rules.body: Extra-bold at 115% width is reserved for the name and section headings. Archivo below them is 700 at normal width.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Interface text is sentence case with no wide tracking. Capitals belong to the name in the form.

rules.name: The Glow Is Matter Rule
rules.body: Glow comes from the particles themselves, through additive light and a soft halo. It never comes from a CSS shadow, a blur or a gradient on an interface element.

rules.name: The Bare Ground Rule
rules.body: Nothing that holds reading text has a panel, card or tint. The navigation bar, the footer and the skip link are filled with Ground itself, so they read as more ground, and they are opaque so the form never passes behind their words.

rules.name: The Square Interface Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the interface takes a radius. The token scale has one step, and it is zero.

rules.name: The Same Matter Rule
rules.body: There is one form and one set of points. A new piece of the site is a new shape for those points, never a second object, model or scene.

rules.name: The Real Shape Rule
rules.body: Every shape is generated from code and, where it shows a quantity, from real data. Experience slabs are as long as each role, Skills columns are as tall as each group, the gear is the same involute profile as the Gear Library, and 3.81 is the actual CGPA.

rules.name: The Readable Words Rule
rules.body: The form never competes with reading. On desktop it dims to 20% at the midpoint of a rebuild, the only time it reaches the words. On phones the words scroll across it, so it steps back to 16% from just after a stop begins until just before the next.

rules.name: The Shed Heaviest First Rule
rules.body: When frame rate declines, the form gives things up one at a time: pixel ratio drops to 1, then the backdrop goes, and only then does the site fall back to Still. A visitor never waits on an effect.

rules.name: The Same Words Rule
rules.body: Every presentation carries the same words in the same order. A fact never lives only in the form: the stage is `aria-hidden`, and nothing in it may be needed to understand the site.

dos: Do set reading text directly on Ground, in Text or Quiet.
Do build each new stop as a shape for the existing points, with an entry in `lib/gallery.ts`, a builder in `components/gallery/form-shapes.ts`, and a matching `data-stop` in the page.
Do derive a shape from real data wherever it shows a quantity.
Do change Ground in `app/globals.css`, `app/layout.tsx`, the canvas, the backdrop and the icon and social images together, since each reads its own copy.
Do recapture both still images in `public/rooms/` whenever a shape or its layout changes.
Do keep the form dimmed wherever it can pass behind words.
Do check every new surface in all three tiers and in list view.
donts: Don't add a second hue, or a cool or pure neutral.
Don't put reading text on a panel, card, tint or blur.
Don't use Amber in the interface for a resting state, or the ember colours in the interface at all.
Don't round a button or any other interface element.
Don't add a CSS shadow or glow to an interface element.
Don't add a second 3D object beside the form, or let a shape fade or cut instead of pouring.
Don't let the burst fire from text or controls, or let the form hold a fact that the words do not.
Don't invent a shape's proportions when real data exists for it.
